decisive_items: Skin biopsy showed dermal neutrophils with upper dermal edema and a subepidermal blister, consistent with bullous Sweet’s syndrome
Five weeks postpartum, she developed a pustular rash on the left upper arm, abdomen, and back
Her blood counts remained low: hemoglobin 13.0 g/dL, white-cell count 1.7×10^9/L (neutrophils 0.5×10^9/L, monocytes 0.1×10^9/L), and platelets 49×10^9/L
response.rationale: The biopsy-confirmed bullous Sweet’s syndrome is the only definitively diagnosed entity among the candidates. The prior ITP was only presumptive and failed steroids and IVIG, while SLE is unsupported by a negative ANA and lack of clinical features. Sweet’s syndrome can occur postpartum and in association with underlying hematologic disorders, fitting the persistent pancytopenia.

rejected.why: Only a family history of SLE is present; ANA was negative and there are no clinical features of SLE.
Immune thrombocytopenia was presumptive and does not explain the neutropenia, monocytopenia, or Sweet’s syndrome; it also failed to respond to steroids and IVIG.
